angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G), matched to the same NFL route families and tested against target-quality-adjusted season separation over expected on held-out draft classes. Positive use: a next-season shortlist rule (SOE > 0, 100+ routes) for day-3 / undrafted receivers, reported as directional only, with Break G shown not to sort it.
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration magnitude (g) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of the first route break, z-scored within drill x Combine year, averaged over route drills and reliability-shrunk; identical code on NFL snaps
headline_number: Held-out slope -1.4 in of target-quality-adjusted season SOE per sd of Break G (90% interval -3.3 to +0.8, n=116; average of plain and ridge forecasts on the same resamples; 90% posterior within +/-3 in). Day-3/UDFA shortlist 6/12 vs 2/8 (gap 25 pts [-14, 58], receiver-clustered; base 40%): directional only.
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_13/cand_2. Football: the lede now refers only to the day-3/UDFA pool (6/12 vs 2/8, gap 25 [-14, 58]) and calls it directional. The all-rounds 62% vs 19% is no longer quoted. All-rounds SOE persistence appears only as context, net of a pick forecast (+0.52 in per in [0.25, 0.73]). New no-SOE baseline: a leave-one-receiver-out forecast from pick, season-1 routes and position picks 3/12 hits; the shortlist adds +14 pts net of it [-28, 50]. Time-forward score: 5/8 vs 1/6 in 2024-25 and 1/4 vs 1/2 in 2023-24. Survival / intent-to-treat check grafted from the DL runner-up (cand_1): 12/16 vs 8/17 reached 100 routes again, and 6/16 vs 2/17 counting drop-outs as misses. The board is cut to the four Figure-1 receivers with route-family coaching (the family with the largest drill-to-NFL Break G drop) and a Boutte clip cue (2024 wk 12 out: 5.2 yd/s in and at the slowest point, 0.33 g, 1.5 yd). New 2026 shortlist table with 13 names, SOE and routes; the 7 soft cutters are flagged as test cases. Holm, Bonferroni, ridge and QB detail moved to a short appendix. Data science: one primary estimate (average of the plain and ridge forecasts on the same 2,000 class-stratified resamples) on SOE adjusted for route mix and depth. Posterior and equivalence statement added. Leave-one-class-out ridge weights shown with intervals (0.52 [-0.45, 3.70], 2.23 [-0.72, 7.34], 1.83 [-0.57, 9.84]). Drill-to-game on the 99 players with 8+ NFL breaks: rho -0.03, reliability-disattenuated -0.09 [-0.70, 0.47]. Nacua-free yards per route run is in the robustness table and is now null (+0.09 [-0.03, 0.24]). Price reconciled: the 14% [5, 23] full-profile held-out price is the only one quoted, and the position-only 9% [2, 17] is renamed price_bg_posonly in numbers.json and explained in the appendix. Writeup: 'Why it matters' rewritten as motivation; one-sentence coach definition; frozen/hashed sentences removed; 'The test' collapsed into a 6-row robustness table; 3-row headline table; 1,795 words by check.py, 1,959 by wc -w. Viz: Figure 1 now shows 4 players in a 2x2 grid; the typical rep is coloured by acceleration through the Break G window; readouts are 13 pt in g and sd; a drill-vs-NFL sd dumbbell replaces the interval strips. The old Figure 4 (forest plus cluttered price-vs-value) is dropped. Figure 3 is cut to 2 panels with the 8+-break correction printed. Figure 2 has its label collisions fixed, is day-3 only in panel B, shows counts by season transition plus the pick-forecast row, and gives the soft/hard split as counts in the caption.
open_risks: The day-3 shortlist result is not significant (gap 25 pts [-14, 58]; 20 pairs from 16 receivers) and went the wrong way in 2023-24 (1/4 vs 1/2); 2026 is its first real test
Choosing target-quality-adjusted SOE as the outcome and averaging the two forecasts was decided this round, after the raw-SOE plain and ridge results were known (all versions are shown)
The disattenuated drill-to-game interval is wide (-0.70 to 0.47), so a moderate transfer is not excluded
The Break G downside is open: losses down to -3.3 in per sd are not excluded
Board route-family reads rest on 1-7 NFL breaks per player, and the Boutte clip is a single play
Game tracking is a 40-play sample per player, half selected for high EPA; the route-mix adjustment uses only the random half
